title: Geofenced Purge Workflow and Compliance Ledger
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Build an automated, region-aware purge workflow that (1) executes deletions according to tenant- and region-specific retention policies, (2) emits tamper-evident, queryable proof of deletion (a compliance ledger), and (3) provides on-demand verification APIs and downloadable deletion receipts for customers and auditors.

Scope: This ticket covers the product-level design and acceptance criteria for the workflow and ledger. Engineering tasks (workers, scheduler, KMS integration, and verification runner) are tracked as dependencies. The feature must handle hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes, respect VPC constraints, and integrate with existing audit logs.

Key requirements:
- Per-tenant retention windows and per-region geofencing rules (e.g., EU-only residency, APAC-specific retention overrides).
- Scheduled and event-driven purge execution (account closure, manual RTBF requests, policy expiry, region-migration).
- A cryptographic, append-only compliance ledger storing deletion attestations (hashes, timestamps, responsible job ID, signed by Redwood KMS/HSM). Ledger must be queryable and exportable for audits.
- Proof/receipt generation: downloadable signed JSON receipts and an API endpoint for third-party verification (verifier key material rotates via KMS).
- Full lifecycle handling: primary data, backups, replicas, derivative artifacts (embeddings, cached prefetches), and model KV cache pointers.
- Idempotent deletion jobs and detection of incomplete purges (retries, backfill jobs).
- Low-latency verification: customers should receive a deletion certificate within SLA (target: 24 hours for standard deletes, 7 days maximum for complex private/on-prem flows).

Trade-offs & constraints:
- Strong consistency across replicated stores can increase purge latency; we will prioritize eventual consistency with strong verification semantics and clear state transitions (e.g., PENDING_DELETION -> DELETING -> DELETED -> ATTESTED).
- Scanning large stores for stale data is resource intensive; propose incremental, checkpointed background workers and a shard-aware scheduler to bound cost.
- Cryptographic ledger and signed receipts add KMS/HSM usage and cost; will require security sign-off and usage quotas.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Pilot: enable for hosted customers in a single region with non-critical tenants; ledger in a read-only export mode.
2) Expand: full ledger emission + verification API for hosted + Dedicated (beta).
3) Private: deliver design and SDK for on-prem ledger deployment w/ optional remote attestation via signed receipts.

Acceptance criteria are below. For implementation details refer to linked design doc and engineering tickets.
updates: 2025-01-15: Initial product scoping workshop with Legal and Security. Legal confirmed proof-of-deletion receipts are required for EU DSARs and some APAC jurisdictions.
2025-01-21: Engineering feasibility sync — consensus on append-only ledger vs third-party ledger; decided to build an internal ledger with optional export to customer S3 for audits.
2025-01-28: UX review: receipts should include minimal identifiers (hashed IDs) to avoid exposing PII in the ledger. Design mock uploaded to Confluence (link below).
2025-02-02: Security review requested (ticket created). KMS key policy draft shared; HSM recommendation pending. Security flagged rotation and key-scope questions.

2025-02-07: Product/ENG trade-off: prefer eventual-consistency purge with explicit verification runs to avoid long tail blocking of user-facing operations. Marcus to propose SLOs for verification latency.
2025-02-12: Updated acceptance criteria and added customer-facing API contract. Design doc (confluence) and engineering task list referenced in links.
acceptance_criteria: Create/Update: Admin UI + API to define per-tenant per-region retention rules and geofencing controls.
Execution: Automated purge jobs trigger per policy event and complete end-to-end for a sample tenant in EU region in the pilot cluster.
Ledger: Compliance ledger contains signed attestations for each completed purge entry; entries provide hash of deleted object, timestamp, job ID, and KMS signature.
Verification: Verification API returns a signed verification object matching the ledger entry; downloadable receipt available within 24 hours for hosted pilot.

Edge cases: System correctly flags and retries deletions for items in failed states (backups, offline replicas), and final attestations are only emitted once deletion is confirmed across configured stores.
Observability: Console shows per-tenant purge status, queue depth, success/failure rates, and verification latency metrics. Alerts configured for failed verification > 4 hours.
Security: KMS key rotation process documented and security sign-off obtained before beta rollout.
notes: Follow-up engineering tasks: ENG-4123 (purge-runner sharding), ENG-5201 (ledger storage + index), ENG-6210 (backups/replica marking).
Coordinate with Customer Success for pilot customers and create an audit-ready export template for legal reviews.
Consider future integration with external attestation services for customers requiring third-party proofs.
